title.fr: Macdonald, Riel et le chemin de fer

text.en: In 1867, Sir John Alexander Macdonald, one of the Fathers of Confederation, became the first Prime Minister of Canada.
text.fr: En 1867, sir John Alexander Macdonald, l'un des Pères de la Confédération, est devenu le premier premier ministre du Canada.

source.quote: In 1867, Sir John Alexander Macdonald, a Father of Confederation, became Canada’s first Prime Minister.

verification.evidence: In 1867, Sir John Alexander Macdonald, a Father of Confederation, became Canada’s first Prime Minister.

text.en: Sir George-Étienne Cartier brought Quebec into Confederation. He also helped work out how the Northwest Territories, Manitoba and British Columbia would join Canada.
text.fr: Sir George-Étienne Cartier a fait entrer le Québec dans la Confédération. Il a aussi aidé à négocier l'entrée des Territoires du Nord-Ouest, du Manitoba et de la Colombie-Britannique au Canada.

source.quote: Cartier led Quebec into Confederation and helped negotiate the entry of the Northwest Territories, Manitoba and British Columbia into Canada.

verification.evidence: Sir George-Étienne Cartier was the key architect of Confederation from Quebec. A railway lawyer, Montrealer, close ally of Macdonald and patriotic Canadien, Cartier led Quebec into Confederation and helped negotiate the entry of the Northwest Territories, Manitoba and British Columbia into Canada.

text.en: When Canada took over the northwest, nobody asked the 12,000 Métis of the Red River what they thought. So Louis Riel led an armed uprising and took Fort Garry, the capital of the territory.
text.fr: Quand le Canada a pris possession du Nord-Ouest, personne n'a consulté les 12 000 Métis de la rivière Rouge. Louis Riel a donc mené un soulèvement armé et s'est emparé de Fort Garry, la capitale du territoire.

source.quote: the 12,000 Métis of the Red River were not consulted. In response, Louis Riel led an armed uprising and seized Fort Garry, the territorial capital.

verification.evidence: When Canada took over the vast northwest region from the Hudson’s Bay Company in 1869, the 12,000 Métis of the Red River were not consulted. In response, Louis Riel led an armed uprising and seized Fort Garry, the territorial capital.

text.en: Riel escaped to the United States, and Canada created a new province called Manitoba.
text.fr: Riel s'est enfui aux États-Unis, et le Canada a créé une nouvelle province appelée le Manitoba.

source.quote: Riel fled to the United States and Canada established a new province: Manitoba.

verification.evidence: Riel fled to the United States and Canada established a new province: Manitoba.

text.en: Many people see Louis Riel as a hero. To them he defended the rights of the Métis, and he is the father of Manitoba.
text.fr: Beaucoup de gens voient Louis Riel comme un héros. Pour eux, il a défendu les droits des Métis, et il est le père du Manitoba.

source.quote: Riel is seen by many as a hero, a defender of Métis rights and the father of Manitoba.

verification.evidence: Riel is seen by many as a hero, a defender of Métis rights and the father of Manitoba.

text.en: Prime Minister Macdonald created the North West Mounted Police (NWMP) in 1873.
text.fr: Le premier ministre Macdonald a créé la Police à cheval du Nord-Ouest en 1873.

source.quote: established the North West Mounted Police (NWMP) in 1873

verification.evidence: After the first Métis uprising, Prime Minister Macdonald established the North West Mounted Police (NWMP) in 1873

text.en: Today the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, the RCMP or “the Mounties,” is Canada's national police force. It is also one of the country's best-known symbols.
text.fr: Aujourd'hui, la Gendarmerie royale du Canada, la GRC ou « la police montée », est le corps de police national du Canada. C'est aussi l'un des symboles les plus connus du pays.

source.quote: Today, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP or “the Mounties”) are the national police force and one of Canada’s best-known symbols.

verification.evidence: Today, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP or “the Mounties”) are the national police force and one of Canada’s best-known symbols.

text.en: British Columbia joined Canada in 1871. It did so after Ottawa promised to build a railway all the way to the West Coast.
text.fr: La Colombie-Britannique s'est jointe au Canada en 1871. Elle l'a fait après qu'Ottawa eut promis de construire un chemin de fer jusqu'à la côte Ouest.

source.quote: British Columbia joined Canada in 1871 after Ottawa promised to build a railway to the West Coast.

verification.evidence: British Columbia joined Canada in 1871 after Ottawa promised to build a railway to the West Coast.

text.en: On November 7, 1885, Donald Smith (Lord Strathcona) drove in the last spike of the Canadian Pacific Railway (CPR). Born in Scotland, he was a director of the CPR. The finished railway was a powerful symbol of unity.
text.fr: Le 7 novembre 1885, Donald Smith (lord Strathcona) a enfoncé le dernier crampon du chemin de fer du Canadien Pacifique (CP). Né en Écosse, il était un administrateur du CP. Le chemin de fer achevé était un puissant symbole d'unité.

source.quote: On November 7, 1885, a powerful symbol of unity was completed when Donald Smith (Lord Strathcona), the Scottish-born director of the Canadian Pacific Railway (CPR), drove the last spike.

verification.evidence: On November 7, 1885, a powerful symbol of unity was completed when Donald Smith (Lord Strathcona), the Scottish-born director of the Canadian Pacific Railway (CPR), drove the last spike.

text.en: After the railway was built, Chinese people faced discrimination. One example was the Head Tax, a fee charged to enter Canada because of race. In 2006, the Government of Canada apologized for this unfair policy.
text.fr: Une fois le chemin de fer construit, les Chinois ont été victimes de discrimination. La taxe d'entrée, un droit à payer pour entrer au Canada imposé en raison de la race, en est un exemple. En 2006, le gouvernement du Canada a présenté des excuses pour cette politique injuste.

source.quote: Afterwards the Chinese were subject to discrimination, including the Head Tax, a race-based entry fee. The Government of Canada apologized in 2006 for this discriminatory policy.

verification.evidence: The project was financed by British and American investors and built by both European and Chinese labour. Afterwards the Chinese were subject to discrimination, including the Head Tax, a race-based entry fee. The Government of Canada apologized in 2006 for this discriminatory policy.

text.en: Sir Wilfrid Laurier was the first French-Canadian prime minister after Confederation.
text.fr: Sir Wilfrid Laurier a été le premier premier ministre canadien-français depuis la Confédération.

source.quote: Sir Wilfrid Laurier became the first French-Canadian prime minister since Confederation

verification.evidence: Sir Wilfrid Laurier became the first French-Canadian prime minister since Confederation
